clue.text: Abed abroad in the dark

definitions.meaning: in French, the language of abroad here
without any lamp or light switched on

explanation.walkthrough: The French for 'a bed' happens to spell the English word for not illuminated.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase for one bed doubles as the English adjective for an unlighted place.

clue.text: Woods are not just like this

definitions.text: Woods are not just like this

parts.words: Woods are not just like this
parts.note: bowls are called woods and are weighted to curve, so they lack fairness in the sense of running straight

explanation.surface: A remark that forests are somehow unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: Woods are the balls in lawn bowls, a British green game; each has a bias, a weighting that makes it curve. 'Just' means fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair and impartial, literally lacking the weighted bias a bowling ball carries.

clue.text: Illuminated note in volume

parts.note: illuminated means lit
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A lit-up musical note appears in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric unit used to measure volume or capacity.

clue.text: Lists of words are thus collected by us

indicators.note: collected means gathered and assembled afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone claims word lists are gathered by us in this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' rearranges the letters of ARE THUS together with US.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference book of synonyms is a set of lists of related words.

clue.text: Presumably it made a lot of Avonville's buildings cleaner

definitions.text: Presumably it made a lot of Avonville's buildings cleaner

parts.words: Presumably it made a lot of Avonville's buildings cleaner
parts.note: Avonville stands for the city of Bath on the Avon; a brick from there might build houses, but this one is a scouring block that cleans

explanation.surface: Musing about the building material of a riverside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English city on the River Avon. A bath brick was a block of fine silt used to scour and polish metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The block named after the spa city was a cleaning abrasive, not building material.

clue.text: Webster's poor broadcast

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so the letters are put in a different arrangement

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a broadcast by a man called Webster as poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges the letters of WEBSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To scatter or strew about, as one sows seed by broadcasting it.

clue.text: Little Arthur rises above himself in Latin journey

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece above another comes first
in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the short name is turned backwards

parts.note: Art is a short form of the name Arthur
ipse is Latin for himself

explanation.surface: Young Arthur gets above himself during a trip to Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns ART upwards into TRA, placed 'above' IPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To trudge wearily on a tiresome trip from place to place.

clue.text: The beef is excellent

explanation.walkthrough: Bully beef is canned corned beef, the British army ration.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinned corned meat is called by this name, and dated slang also uses it for first-rate.

clue.text: Simulated take-off

definitions.meaning: a take-off is a parody or impression of someone

explanation.definitionFit: Fake goods are this kind, and a mimic's impression is one.

clue.text: Leading journalist in a state of tension

parts.note: key means principal or leading
ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A top reporter is under stress.
explanation.definitionFit: Keyed up means nervously tense and excited.

clue.text: Knocks every dog's home in London

parts.note: batters means knocks or pounds
ea is short for each, every

explanation.surface: Someone thumps every dog's kennel in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Battersea Dogs Home is a famous animal shelter in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: A London district best known for its rescue shelter for stray dogs.

clue.text: Not a clerical body in Italy, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A remark that Italy may not be governed by the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the letters of ITALY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary churchgoers as distinct from ordained clergy.

clue.text: A period return, say, to Wembley

indicators.note: return means come back, so the phrase is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the article a becomes an before a vowel
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An era of football comes back to Wembley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reads AN ERA backwards. 'say' marks Wembley, the London stadium, as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Wembley Stadium is an example of a large sports venue.

clue.text: Sort of message one responds freely to

definitions.text: Sort of message one responds freely to

parts.words: Sort of message one responds freely to
parts.note: a telegram whose answer has been prepaid by the sender, so the recipient answers at no cost

explanation.surface: Describing a note you can answer without cost.
explanation.walkthrough: Old telegrams and letters could be sent with the cost of the response already paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram with its response prepaid lets the receiver answer at no charge.

clue.text: Slipway to dilapidated part of US town

definitions.meaning: a skid road was a track along which logs were slid
a run-down district of vagrants and drunks

explanation.definitionFit: Originally a logging track for sliding timber; later a seedy American district of down-and-outs.

clue.text: Kind of heater required for baptism

definitions.meaning: an electric water heater in a tank
baptism by total dipping under water

explanation.walkthrough: An immersion heater warms water in a British home's hot tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A tank water heater has this name, and so does dipping someone under water.

clue.text: The sort of man Rackstraw was, to his credit

definitions.text: The sort of man Rackstraw was, to his credit

parts.words: The sort of man Rackstraw was, to his credit
parts.note: Ralph Rackstraw in Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore is praised in a song for his nationality

explanation.surface: A tribute to a character's nationality.
explanation.walkthrough: In HMS Pinafore the chorus sings that 'he is an Englishman', and 'it is greatly to his credit'.
explanation.definitionFit: The sailor's nationality, celebrated in the operetta's song as being from England.

clue.text: Sort of feat performed on horseback

definitions.text: Sort of feat performed on horseback

parts.words: Sort of feat performed on horseback
parts.note: the horse is the vaulting horse in a gym, not a live animal

explanation.surface: Describing a stunt rider's trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'horse' is the pommel or vaulting horse used in athletic competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Feats on a pommel horse belong to athletic exercises.

clue.text: Eagle-featured, one-armed Captain snooped

parts.note: Captain Hook in Peter Pan lost a hand to the crocodile
nosed means pried or snooped

explanation.surface: The beak-faced pirate went poking around.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a curved, beak-like nose like an eagle's.

clue.text: A manor house and land, humble some say

indicators.note: some speakers pronounce the word so it is heard like another

parts.note: demean means humble or degrade

explanation.surface: An estate described as modest, according to some.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some say' marks a sound-alike for those who pronounce the estate word to rhyme with mean.
explanation.definitionFit: The land attached to a manor and kept for the owner's own use.

clue.text: Removal time guaranteed

parts.note: an era is a time or age
sure means certain or guaranteed

explanation.surface: A removal date is promised.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing out or deleting something removes it.

clue.text: Fruit religious individuals take to

parts.note: pi is short for pious, religious
men means people or individuals

explanation.surface: Pious people adopt a certain fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet red pepper, botanically a fruit.

clue.text: Kind of concrete that takes woven carpets

indicators.note: woven means interlaced, so the letters are worked into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A concrete that somehow absorbs woven rugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' rearranges the letters of CARPETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete moulded into shape before going on site.

clue.text: Scuttle along on the boundary line like a mad thing

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it

parts.note: a march is a border or frontier
to hare is to run fast

explanation.surface: Someone scurries along a border like a madman.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal is proverbially 'mad as a March hare', and a mad one appears at the tea party in Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: The springtime animal is a proverbial symbol of madness.

clue.text: Code name of spymaster brought up in France

indicators.note: in a down clue bringing up means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A spy chief's code name raised in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reads CODE M backwards; 'name of' links. The definition is loose: a region found in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a wine region near Bordeaux in south-west France.

clue.text: Rustic individual's language

parts.note: a hind is a farm labourer or rustic
I, the Roman one, stands for a single individual

explanation.surface: A country fellow's way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A major tongue of northern India.

clue.text: Continue to pose as an historian

indicators.note: to here means attached to, so the first piece is added onto the end of the second

parts.note: to act is to pose or pretend
on, as in carry on, means continue

explanation.surface: Someone keeps on pretending to be a historian.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Acton was a Victorian historian, famous for 'power tends to corrupt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Acton was a noted English historian of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Secure rope when riding

parts.note: to tie is to rope or bind
up means on horseback, riding

explanation.surface: Fasten a rope while on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten firmly or moor a boat.

clue.text: Soundly bottled spirit

indicators.note: soundly means as heard, so the word is spoken and written another way

parts.note: gin is a spirit sold in bottles

explanation.surface: A spirit sealed in a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud it matches a drink sold in bottles, and a genie is a spirit famously kept in a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A genie of Arabian lore, often imagined trapped in a lamp or flask.

clue.text: Girl gym head's lack of qualification

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
PT is physical training, done in the gym
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A girl who runs the gym is unqualified.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsuitability, being ill-fitted for a role.

clue.text: The mainland is temperate

definitions.meaning: the European landmass as seen from Britain

explanation.definitionFit: Britons call mainland Europe by this name, and it also means self-restrained.

clue.text: Three coppers arrest one boy, shooter

indicators.note: arrest means hold, so the outer letters grip the inner

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
p is a penny, a copper coin
d stood for the old British penny, a copper coin
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Three policemen detain one young gunman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrest' puts I inside CU, P and D. D was the symbol for a pre-1971 British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of love is a boy archer.
